epsilon.note: Declared 2026-08-31 from a preprint-v3 measurement on a 2g.20gb MIG slice against full-H100 baselines. Kept at 0.025 on 2026-09-26 for re-runs on the declared GPU, where a re-run of the same code reproduces the baseline exactly; a delta inside epsilon therefore means code or data drift that stays small. Real substrate drift (wrong splits/features/labels) manifests at >=0.05.

gpu.note: Discovery folds 0-2 re-run at one commit on a full H100 and on a 3g.40gb MIG slice. The same GPU type gave identical predictions in every check, across nodes and jobs. The two GPU types gave different predictions on every fold; the largest per-fold gap was 0.045 (ABMIL), 0.033 (CLAM) and 0.018 (DTFD-MIL). Every run of a cell is compared against its baseline, so every run of a runtime set trains on the GPU type declared for it.

gpu_rtx_6000_ada.note: Discovery folds 0-2 re-run on an RTX 6000 Ada and compared with the full-H100 baselines of fir. Predictions differed on all 12 folds; the largest per-fold gap was 0.043 (ABMIL), above epsilon, while an RTX repeat of ABMIL reproduced the first RTX run bit for bit. H100 baselines therefore cannot anchor RTX runs: runtime-aihub trains its own baselines on the RTX. It is a rehearsal set; official cells run on fir.
